name: Modeling of Pavement Materials
description: Role of constitutive modeling; laboratory testing in relation to constitutive modeling: elastic modulus, resilient modulus, complex modulus, creep, rheological tests; introduction to continuum mechanics: strain tensor, stress tensor, isotropy, anisotropy, constitutive relationships; factors affecting material behavior: temperature, rate, time, confining pressure; unbound materials: soil, aggregate; bound materials: binding using asphalt, water, lime, polymer, flyash, cement; rheology: bituminous binder; constitutive models: unbound materials, bound materials; field performance of pavement materials: fatigue, rutting, temperature issues, moisture damage, permeability; transfer functions to relate laboratory performance with field performance.
